newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RESEARCH ALERT - Hungary power firm Elmu rated "buy".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hungary power firm Elmu rated "buy".

text.p: London-based ICE Securities said that Elmu, the electricity distributor supplying Budapest, is potentially the most profitable of Hungary's regional distribution companies, rating its OTC-traded shares as "buy".

"Elmu... is the largest and potentially the most efficient and profitable among the electricity supply companies that can provide a simple, but effective portfolio hedge in a volatile Hungarian market," ICE's analyst Rudi Voros said in a report.
The analyst said he saw clear signs that Elmu's new management was unlocking the company's hidden potential through a rapid restructuring programme.
"Therefore, Elmu is our number one choice of all the electricity supply companies that are coming to the market, and accordingly, we recommend purchases," he said in the report, dated May 7.
Elmu is 46.15 percent owned by the German consortium of RWE and EVS which paid a 75 percent premium above the face value for the stake.
On the Hungarian over-the-counter market Hungarian brokers are publishing bids and offers for Elmu shares at between 88 percent and 104 percent of the face value.
In 1996 Elmu posted a loss of 3.04 billion forints, caused partly by October's cancelled energy price rises.
"Thus far the company's profitability has been negatively influenced by the de facto and the current quasi subsidisation of electricity prices," Voros said.

"Despite the widely accepted perception that Elmu is the most advanced among the six electricity suppliers, in 1997 the company is certain to fall short of the eight percent return on equity which was promised by the government at the time of the first round of utility privatisation."
But for next year ICE expects a turnaround in this respect.
"We believe that the company should be earning an eight percent return by the end of 1998, by which time the major part of the restructuring process should be complete," Voros said.
"Thereafter, we believe, the company will provide predictable but inflation-proof earnings growth..."
ICE expects a net profit of 3.1 billion forints for 1997, six billion for 1998 and 7.3 billion for 1999.
